title: Introduce variable-contrast anchors and radius flow for form-factor modes
creator: Marina Valdez
description: Bring a cohesive token strategy that supports two primary form-factor modes (Compact and Comfortable) with clear contrast anchors and progressive radius/spacing rules across buttons, tables, and charts. This ticket scopes the token definitions, migration guidance, and a conservative rollout that preserves accessibility and backward compatibility for existing UIs.
background: Multiple teams have implemented local token deltas to support compact UIs and denser tables; this has led to visual drift and duplicated CSS/runtime overrides. Recent accessibility reviews flagged inconsistent contrast ramps in dense mode, and engineering has requested a simple mapping that can be computed at build/runtime. We need a single source of truth for: color contrast anchors (foreground/background pairs), a variable radius/spacing flow for breakpoints and density, and an elevation/shadow grammar that scales with perceived depth without increasing contrast violations.
proposal: Create a variable token layer: base tokens -> density modifiers -> component deltas. Base tokens define neutral palette stems, type scale, and base spacing. Density modifiers (compact/comfortable) adjust spacing, radius and shadow amplitude using percentage deltas and clamp rules. Component deltas are minimal overrides that map to the final computed values. Implement the tokens as CSS variables + JSON token export. Provide migration helpers for legacy CSS classes and a runtime shim for Redwood Console to toggle density per-route.
token_changes: Introduce color anchors: anchor-foreground-1..3 and anchor-background-1..3 with WCAG targets per anchor
Add density modifiers: density.compact.* and density.comfortable.* for spacing, radius, and shadow-scale
Introduce radius-flow tokens: radius-base, radius-step-01..04 and density multipliers
Refactor elevation to shadow-scale tokens: shadow-amplitude-0..5 with density-adjustable blur/spread
Expose a computed token export for runtime (JSON) and CSS var fallback path for older clients
tradeoffs_and_considerations: Compute-at-build vs runtime: build-time favors smaller payloads; runtime offers toggling per-session. We'll provide both but default to build-time exports.
Strict WCAG anchoring reduces expressive extremes for brand colors; we'll provide brand color aliases that map to anchors at specific contrast levels.
Keeping component deltas minimal reduces churn for consumers but may not capture every legacy visual — include a migration guide for edge cases.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical token JSON and CSS var bundle published under design-tokens-2026.03
Component library (buttons, table cells, chart legends) renders both Compact and Comfortable modes with visual parity to mocks within 2px/2pt tolerances
Automated contrast checks ensure anchor pairs meet specified WCAG thresholds for text sizes used
Migration helper script converts at least 90% of existing token references in core repo without manual edits
Docs and examples in the component playground showing toggle between densities and explaining token mapping

rollout_plan: Week 1: Finalize spec and publish alpha token bundle to internal registry
Week 2: Integrate tokens into component library, enable playground density toggle
Week 3: Ship migration helper and run codemods on 2 pilot repos, collect regressions
Week 4: Iterate on fixes, publish v1 tokens behind feature flag for Console
Week 5: Lift flag after smoke tests and accessibility sign-off
qa_checks: Visual diff across 6 viewport sizes for each component in both densities
Contrast report shows no regressions vs baseline for body and button text
Performance: CSS payload size increase < 3% for default bundle
Component snapshot tests updated and passing
